1 صَمَرَ , (M, K,) aor.
صَمُرَ , (M,) inf. n. صَمْرٌ and صُمُورٌ, He was niggardly, or tenacious, and refused; (M, K;) as also ↓ اصمر , and ↓ صمّر : (K:) [or] صَمَرَ, inf. n. صَمْرٌ, signifies he collected, and refused; and so ↓ اصمر , and ↓ صمّر : one says, صَمَرَ مَتَاعَهُ [he collected, and refused, his goods]: (O:) [but ISd says that] the phrase ↓ الصَّامِرِينَ مَتَاعَهُمْ, used by a poet, means, الصَّامِرِينَ بِمَتَاعِهِمْ [i. e., accord. to the context, those who are niggardly with their goods]. (M.) ＝
-A2- صَمَرَ المَآءُ, (M, O, K,) aor.
صَمُرَ , inf. n. صُمُورٌ, (M, O,) The water ran from a declivity into a level place, and then became calm, or tranquil, while [continuing] running. (M, O, K.) And ↓ صِمْرٌ signifies The resting-place of such water: (M, K:) and ↓ صِمْرُ الوَادِى the resting-place of such water of the valley. (TA.) ＝
-A3- صَمَرَ, (O, K,) aor.
صَمِرَ ; (K;) and صَمِرَ, (O, K,) aor.
صَمَرَ ; (K;) said of milk, (O, K,) It was, or became, sour; (O;) or very sour; as also ↓ اصمر . (O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
